checks.invariant: Agent-grown audit rows have an aggregate bound or retention, so one prompt-injected agent cannot grow the shared SQLite file without limit; a per-record cap on args is not an effective bound.
checks.result: AuditLog fixture: 40 tool-call record pairs written with the largest args the audit path accepts (exec command of 80,000 bytes -> args_head exactly 16,384 bytes) added 30,076 bytes per call; the same pairs with {command: ls} added 9,476 bytes per call; growth is linear and no code path ever removes rows. DELETE FROM audit and UPDATE audit are both rejected by the append-only triggers ('audit log is append-only'). grep shows no retention, VACUUM, size or count quota for the audit table anywhere in agentbox/. service.py:182-183 states the authors' own premise that this log cannot be deleted and that an agent growing it is irreversible.

checks.invariant: Approval rows (which hold the full, unmasked agent args) are size-bounded and are removed on decision, expiry and sandbox deletion.
checks.result: ApprovalStore on the same DB file stored 400,000-byte exec args as 416,120 bytes per row (5 rows). No DELETE FROM approvals exists anywhere in agentbox/ (the only prunes are ui_tickets/ui_sessions/takeover_leases in desktop.py), and the delete path only unlinks capture PNGs (service.py:106-109, 471-475). Rows therefore survive approve/deny/expire and sandbox deletion. web.py:206-211 loads every historical row with full args/preview JSON every 2 s per open UI page and keeps the last 5, so retained rows also amplify read work.

checks.invariant: Human audit read paths clamp their cost on the shared audit lock (limit is an upper bound, not a hint).
checks.result: api.py:269 applies min(limit, 5000), which does not clamp negatives: list(limit=-1) returned all 160 rows of the fixture (SQLite LIMIT -1 means no limit), so a single GET /audit?limit=-1 would decode the whole table into memory while holding AuditLog._lock. Reachable only with the human bearer token (api.py:115-129), so this is an operator self-cost rather than a cross-principal attack.

checks.invariant: Read-side lock hold on the single audit lock is O(window), so monitoring reads cannot stall every agent append as the table grows.
checks.result: recent() performs COUNT(*) plus the sandbox-filtered ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 400 inside 'with self._lock' (audit.py:212-217); verify() does fetchall of the whole table inside the same lock (audit.py:225-228); the SCHEMA creates no index besides the INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (audit.py:23-34), so the sandbox filter and status scan are full scans. audit.py:158-186 shows append needs that same lock. templates/sandbox.html:19 re-issues /ui/audit every 3 s and web.py:265-269 serves it, so each open sandbox page holds the append lock for a full-table COUNT(*) every 3 s; growth caused by the agent therefore lengthens a lock hold that blocks the agent's own fail-closed appends.

checks.invariant: Audit-write failure is fail-closed before execution and cannot silently discard the only record of an action (GUI burst changes and stray kills) after it ran.
checks.result: Harness on the real AgentBox.log_best_effort with an audit stub that raises: AuditWriteError is swallowed after exactly one append attempt and no record is written; a RuntimeError from append is not swallowed and escapes. gui_bursts.py:107-111 deletes self._gui_burst[sid] before _finish() calls self._log (gui_bursts.py:130-135, 90-92), so a swallowed failure leaves no gui_changes/gui_processes_stopped row and no retry state. Fail-closed holds for the next call (service.py:295-306, 590-594 raise 503), and handback/takeover/export refuse to proceed without a record (service.py:536-541, 497-500).

checks.invariant: Rejected agent requests cannot add uncapped rows to the audit log.
checks.result: api.py:252-259 appends an approval_forbidden row for every agent attempt to POST /approvals/{aid} and swallows only append errors, so this is one more agent-driven row source with no rate or count bound; it feeds the same unbounded table as tool calls.

checks.invariant: Approval state cannot remain in a non-terminal state after a partial failure (claim-then-execute is recoverable).
checks.result: decide() claims the row to 'approved' (approvals.py:82-89) before snapshot and execution (service.py:395-418). Every exception path calls finish(FAILED), but a control-plane crash or OOM between claim and finish leaves the row 'approved' forever: expire_stale only scans PENDING (service.py:375-388), so nothing ever revisits it and the agent's GET /approvals/{aid} reports an approval that never executed. No privilege effect; recovery gap only.

unresolved: Host volume free space, expected deployment lifetime and any operator-side retention for data/agentbox.db are outside the repository; the product itself can never delete audit rows without permanently breaking /audit/verify.

checks.invariant: Timeline readers show the newest rows and the true total, or page until the newest row (run-3 root cause: list() oldest-first with limit=5000 treated as the newest window).
checks.result: Fixture with 1,000 rows: recent(sandbox, limit=400) returned ids 1000..601 newest-first with total=1000, so /ui/audit (web.py:268) now shows the newest window and the real count; templates/_audit.html:10 only claims '최근 N개만 표시 (전체 M개)' when total exceeds the window, so it no longer misrepresents a truncated tail. list() is still oldest-first (ids 1..1000) but cli.py:254-260 now pages with after_id = rows[-1]['id'] until an empty page, which reached id 1000 with 1,000 rows. The run-3 root cause no longer holds for either reader.

checks.invariant: GET /audit limit accepts only a bounded value.
checks.result: min(limit, 5000) at api.py:269 evaluates min(-1, 5000) = -1 and AuditLog.list passed limit straight into 'LIMIT ?': list(limit=-1) returned all 160 fixture rows. The recon lead is confirmed as a source fact, but the route uses human_only (api.py:265-269, 126-129), which only the shared human bearer token satisfies, so it is an operator-only cost and not an agent or session boundary crossing.

checks.invariant: Agent-controlled content cannot erase or rewrite its own audit history, and rows cannot be attributed to another actor.
checks.result: DELETE and UPDATE on audit were rejected by the append-only triggers (local fixture), and audit.py:35-38 defines them as the only write guards. actor is server-assigned from the resolved principal (api.py:220 passes p.kind, which is 'agent' or 'human' from the token, api.py:115-124) and tool is validated against TOOLS before any row is written (service.py:291-296), so an agent cannot forge a human or system row, reorder ids (ids are contiguous, audit.py:165-167) or hide a later action.

checks.invariant: CLI audit paging terminates and cannot livelock.
checks.result: after_id advances to the last id of each page and the loop breaks on an empty page (cli.py:255-260); ids are strictly increasing, so the loop terminates at the newest row. The remaining cost is client-side memory in the operator's own process (all pages accumulate in 'rows'), which is not a shared-service effect.

checks.invariant: mask_text masks well-formed credential shapes in every string payload value before persistence.
checks.result: A DSN inside a command ('psql postgresql://admin:S3cretPw0rd@db/app') was masked by _URL_CRED when the args were not truncated, and the human token is covered both by register_secret (api.py:86-88) and by the (agt|hum)_ token pattern (audit.py:69).

checks.invariant: Masking applies to the whole accepted argument blob, not to a pre-truncated prefix.
checks.result: Recon lead confirmed: _logged_args slices the JSON blob to 16,384 bytes and stores that head (service.py:189-194) before AuditLog._mask/mask_text ever runs (audit.py:160). With the same DSN ending exactly at the cut, the head ends with 'postgresql://admin:S3cretPw0rd', its '@' is dropped by the cut, _URL_CRED no longer matches, and the complete password survived masking into the append-only log; the identical untruncated command was masked. Partial tokens split at the cut (e.g. 'ghp_') also survive. Masking is an anti-accident control (a hostile agent can split any secret across values), so this is a hardening gap rather than a boundary failure.

checks.invariant: _mask covers every container a secret can sit in, including dict keys and non-str leaves.
checks.result: Recon lead confirmed: _mask recurses dict values and list items but returns keys unchanged (audit.py:137-147), so {'password=hunter2': 'v'} keeps the key verbatim. Every server-built payload uses fixed key names; only tool_request args carry agent-chosen keys (service.py:296), so the unmasked key is data the agent itself supplied and no human secret can reach a key. Hardening note only.

checks.invariant: Control-plane tokens are registered as secrets and never persist in the log in clear.
checks.result: The human token is registered before any append (api.py:86-88) and each sandbox token right after creation (service.py:436), and the token patterns in audit.py:58-70 additionally cover agt_/hum_ values of 16+ characters, so a token echoed into args, stdout_head or an error message is masked even if registration were missed.

checks.invariant: A failure inside the masking step cannot fall back to writing unmasked payloads or a broken chain.
checks.result: payload is masked at audit.py:160 before BEGIN IMMEDIATE and before the INSERT, and the hash is computed over the masked record (audit.py:169-184); an exception in masking aborts the append without a row, so there is no no-crypto fallback. The defect is only that such an exception is not converted to AuditWriteError (it escapes as a raw exception), which the unit-1 harness observed.

candidates.title: Agent-grown audit and approval rows in the shared control-plane SQLite file have no aggregate bound or retention, so an agent can fill the host disk and the only recovery breaks the audit chain
candidates.description: Every agent tool call appends two audit rows (tool_request, policy_decision) and risky calls add an approval_requested row plus an approvals-table row; args are capped per record but nothing bounds the tables, and no code path deletes audit rows. A prompt-injected agent that loops allowed tool calls with 80 KB arguments adds about 30 KB per call to data/agentbox.db on the host volume, permanently. When the volume fills, AuditLog.append raises AuditWriteError, which service.py converts to 503 for tool calls, human lifecycle, approvals and handbacks, so the whole control plane stops rather than only the offending sandbox. The only way to reclaim space (deleting old audit rows or the file) permanently trips the id/prev_hash checks, so capacity recovery and audit integrity cannot both be kept.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The audit table is append-only by design (audit.py:35-38) and the per-record arg cap (service.py:37-38, 181-194) is the only bound on agent-driven growth; there is no aggregate quota, retention window, pruning command or size check, and approvals rows holding the full unmasked args are likewise never deleted. The shared SQLite file used by all four components (api.py:86-94, config.py:85-86) therefore has host disk as its only limit, and audit.py:229-236 rejects any prefix deletion, so the recovery path and the integrity contract are mutually exclusive.

trace.description: An agent token calls a tool with agent-controlled body.args; api.py has no request-body cap for tool args (only the upload route at api.py:278-283 is capped).
tool_request is appended with _logged_args(args) and policy_decision is appended right after; both happen before any snapshot or execution.
Only the single record is bounded: blobs over 64 KiB are replaced by a 16 KiB head plus size and sha256, measured at 30,076 bytes per two-row call.
REQUIRE_APPROVAL stores the full raw args and preview in the approvals table (approvals.py:49-59); PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX=20 limits concurrency only, and expired or decided rows are never removed.
The row is inserted into the same SQLite file; the append-only triggers at audit.py:35-38 make it permanent and there is no retention job in the repository.
At disk-full every append raises AuditWriteError, which becomes 503 for human lifecycle, import/export and tool calls, so the blast radius is all sandboxes rather than the agent's own process.
Reclaiming space by deleting the oldest rows makes the first surviving row fail the expected_id or prev_hash check, so /audit/verify reports a broken chain permanently after any capacity recovery.

evidence.description: Append-only triggers abort every UPDATE and DELETE; the local fixture reproduced both rejections.
verify() requires ids to start at 1 and each prev_hash to chain, so prefix deletion is indistinguishable from tampering.
LOGGED_ARGS_MAX/LOGGED_ARGS_HEAD are the only size controls and they are per record, not per table or per sandbox.
The author comment states the log cannot be deleted and that an agent growing it with large args cannot be undone.
drop_captures removes only capture PNGs; approval rows, their full args and preview survive sandbox deletion.
snapshot_quota exists specifically so an agent cannot fill host disk with docker commits without a human, showing the intended invariant that agent actions are host-disk bounded.
create() stores the full raw args JSON with no cap; the fixture measured 416,120 bytes for 400 KB args and no deletion path exists.
AuditLog, SandboxManager, ApprovalStore and DesktopControl share one file, settings.db_path (config.py:85-86, default ./data/agentbox.db).
Each 2-second UI poll materialises every historical approval row with full args and preview, so retained rows also cost control-plane memory and DB read time.

blockers: Free space on the host volume holding data/agentbox.db and the deployment's expected lifetime are outside the repository; no size quota or disk check exists in code (config.py:85-86).

Whether operators prune or rotate the SQLite file out of band is a deployment fact; the product cannot do it without permanently failing /audit/verify, so the acceptable trade-off is an owner decision.

validation_plan.local: Already performed and retained as agents/h-audit/artifacts/h.out: 80 records in a scratch DB measured 30,076 bytes per max-size tool call and 9,476 bytes per 'ls' call, DELETE/UPDATE rejected by the triggers, and 5 approval rows of 400 KB args measured 416,120 bytes each.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on a disposable deployment: record free space on the data/agentbox.db volume, run 1,000 allowed exec calls from one agent token with 80 KB commands, then compare the DB size delta with the free-space budget and confirm whether any operator retention or rotation exists for that file.

hardening: GET /audit applies min(limit, 5000) without a lower clamp (api.py:269); limit=-1 becomes SQL LIMIT -1 and returned the whole table in the local fixture. It is human-token only (api.py:126-129), so it is an operator self-cost; fix with max(1, min(limit, 5000)).

AuditLog.recent() runs COUNT(*) and a sandbox-filtered full scan (no index except the primary key, audit.py:23-34) inside the same lock that append() needs (audit.py:212-217, 158-186); /ui/audit is re-issued every 3 s per open page (templates/sandbox.html:19, web.py:265-269), so a large table lengthens a lock hold that blocks agent appends rather than failing fast.

approvals_view loads every historical approval row with full args/preview JSON twice (web.py:207-209) on a 2-second poll and keeps five, so approval retention multiplies control-plane memory and DB read work.

AgentBox.log_best_effort swallows AuditWriteError but lets other exceptions escape (service.py:366-372); the local harness showed a RuntimeError propagating after execution. AuditLog._mask iterates self._secrets without a lock while register_secret mutates it (audit.py:133-145) and raises before the try block, so that race becomes an unhandled 500 and a lost post-hoc record. Copy the set or guard it.

Masking runs after truncation: _logged_args cuts the blob to 16 KiB (service.py:189-194) and audit.py:160 masks only that head, so a complete credential whose delimiter falls past the cut persists (measured with postgresql://admin:S3cretPw0rd). Mask the full blob first, then truncate, and add a boundary regression fixture.

_mask rewrites values only, never dict keys (audit.py:137-147); the local fixture kept {'password=hunter2': ...} verbatim. Only tool_request args have agent-chosen keys today, so no human secret reaches a key, but masking keys costs nothing.

Approval rows are never deleted (not on decide, expire or sandbox delete; service.py:106-109, 471-475) although capture PNGs are, so the deleted-sandbox approval queue keeps raw args and previews forever in the same file.

decide() claims a row to 'approved' before snapshot and execution (approvals.py:82-89, service.py:395-418); a crash between claim and finish leaves it 'approved' forever because expire_stale only scans PENDING (service.py:379), so an agent can read a status for an action that never ran.

uncovered.surface: Approval queue rows as an alternate, unmasked reader copy of tool args, retained after decide/expire/sandbox delete
uncovered.boundary: agentbox/approvals.py storage and retention versus the masking policy enforced for the audit log; SQLite file retention across sandbox deletion
uncovered.reason: No assigned unit owns approval-table retention: the audit units own the hash chain and masking of audit rows, and the delete/lifecycle unit owns ordering and capture PNGs. It needs its own deterministic unit to decide whether the never-deleted raw-args row (including after the sandbox is gone) is intended audit history or an unmasked derived copy that outlives the workspace it describes.
